title: Grateful Dead Live at Pirates World on 1970-03-24
lineage: SBD > Master Reel > Cassette > DAT (44.1k) > Sony R500 > SEK'D Prodif Plus > Samplitude v8.01 Professional > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: Crisp, well‑balanced soundboard capture of a fireworks‑filled 1970 Pirates World show featuring a soaring Dark Star and blistering Good Lovin’ jams.
ai_review.review: The recording is an excellent SBD mix with clear instrument separation, just a few splice/cut quirks that don’t detract from the listening experience. Musically the night is a highlight of the early‑70 era – tight transitions, a cosmic Dark Star, fiery Don't Ease Me In and a monster Good Lovin’ keep the energy high from start to finish.

ai_rating.rationale: Over twenty enthusiastic reviews praise both performance and sound quality; minor splice/cut issues are outweighed by consistently strong musical remarks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clear, well‑balanced SBD with crisp highs and tight lows; a splice at Dark Star 5:02 and the first few seconds of Morning Dew are missing, but overall no hiss or noise complaints.

standout_songs: High Time > Dark Star > The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers note tight transitions (e.g., Lovelight → Uncle) and a festival‑energy flow; songs are concise yet inspired, keeping the momentum high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for fiery guitar leads, dueling solos with Bob, and emotive vocals on Cold Rain/High Time; described as 'on fire' and 'soulful'.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned for sounding like a different instrument during Dark Star jams and providing deep rhythmic support.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for his dueling guitar work with Jerry on the Morning Dew jam and overall strong rhythm playing.
band_member_comments.Drums: Described as machine‑gun/locomotive power; drum solo called appropriate and not overly long, with both Bill and Mickey noted.
